page: Microsoft Azure DC48as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and standard AVX. The server provides no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage volumes.

Benchmark results place the DC48as_v5 consistently within the average middle 50 percent tier of its compute class. In CPU stress evaluations via stress-ng, the server recorded a single-core score of 2332.97 and a multi-core score of 55581.86. Memory and network transaction testing via Redis yielded 47.03 million SET operations per second, similarly aligning with the mid-range performance bracket. Vector instruction processing is limited to standard AVX, lacking AVX-512 and matrix multiplication extensions.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture standpoint, the instance trades local disk access for external storage flexibility, necessitating careful sizing of network-attached block storage for I/O-intensive workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation and proportional memory footprint make the DC48as_v5 suitable for multi-threaded application servers, distributed Redis caching tiers, background task processing, and relational database deployments configured with external persistent storage.
description: Microsoft Azure DC48as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 24-core, 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per thread. The server provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached Premium Storage for persistent file systems, and includes zero discrete GPUs. Hardware acceleration includes AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic primitives, alongside standard AVX extensions. Synthetic benchmark results locate the system in the middle 50 percent bracket, achieving 2332.97 on stress-ng single-core, 55581.86 on stress-ng multi-core, and 47.03 million SET operations per second in Redis tests. The DC48as_v5 is designed for balanced enterprise workloads, distributed caching tiers, and multi-threaded business applications.
